answer: Because the island stake is held until the forge settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the timber audit lists each exposure. An attester must stake 20% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer costs proportionally more than endorsing a inexpensive one. A farm running 97 keys as a result burns that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation trivial. That is 39 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
